about: Zones a city sets for shared e-scooters, read from the layers of its public map: where to park, where not to, where to ride slowly and where not to ride. Some state a licence for theirs: Alexandria, Rostock, Stockholm and Tampa CC0, Basel, Braunschweig, Helsinki, Namur, Rīga, Taupō, Turku, Vantaa and Wien CC BY 4.0, Cleveland the ODbL, Berlin the Datenlizenz Deutschland – Zero 2.0, Bordeaux Métropole the Licence Ouverte, Aachen, Hamburg, München and Münster the Datenlizenz Deutschland – Namensnennung 2.0, St. Albert its Open Data License, Santa Monica ODC-By 1.0, San Francisco's SFMTA the ODC Public Domain Dedication and License, Vancouver the Open Government Licence – Vancouver, the City of London the Open Government Licence v3.0, Lambeth too for its website, and Washington CC BY 4.0 for its corrals and no-parking zones; since 28 October 2026 public city layers are drawn without one too, credited to the city, and since 1 November 2026 a public zone map the city points to: Stavanger's are the zones Nivel's platform serves to the map the kommune's page embeds, Long Beach's and Nashville's the shapes of the cities' policies on Populus's public policy map, which each city links, and Nashville's corrals the symbols of Metro's PDF map of them (17 March 2025), placed by the PDF's own georeference. Since 10 November 2026 a city's terms do not hold its layers back either, where they allow only personal or non-commercial use or ask for its written permission first: Austin's, Augsburg's, Budapest's, Denver's, Düsseldorf's, Kassel's, Kraków's, Le Chesnay-Rocquencourt's, Leeds's, Lisboa's, Mülheim an der Ruhr's, Nürnberg's, Orlando's, Phoenix's, Plymouth's, Roma's, Stuttgart's, the University of Florida's and Vilnius's are drawn so, each credited. Long Beach's parking drop zones, which the City gives the operators alone, are not drawn. A city whose map stops answering keeps the zones last read from it. Taupō's and Namur's operations areas, where their scooters may go at all, are not drawn. Namur's zones where a scooter may be parked only in a reserved place are drawn as such, only on the website, as Helsingborg's centre, Braunschweig's old town within the Oker, the London Borough of Lambeth, Poznań's zone of Hop & Go points, Stavanger's inner centre, Long Beach's beach path, Budapest's micromobility zones, Kraków's area of mobility points, Vilnius's restricted parking zone, the zones round Düsseldorf's sharing stations, Nürnberg's city within the Bundesstraßenring (its old town, within it, not drawn again), Kassel's Innenstadtring, Plymouth's and Leeds's Beryl areas, Orlando's Lake Nona and the University of Florida's campus are. Kassel publishes no shape of its ring: it is traced on OpenStreetMap (© OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL) along the streets the city names, and the racks within it, where a scooter is parked only on 27 marked places the city does not publish, are not drawn. Oslo's school yards, no-riding on weekdays only, are not drawn: only its zones of every day are. Bordeaux Métropole's places for bikes or mopeds alone are not drawn, nor Trondheim's zones that cap the operators' fleets in its centre and its south, nor Aachen's parking areas not yet set up (vorläufig). San Francisco's are the five zones of SFMTA's parking restrictions from 1 October 2025: the zones they replaced on the Embarcadero and at Pier 40, still in its data without an end, are not drawn, nor those it set for APEC's week or an event. Each city's zones are in data/city-zones/<id>.json, written by scripts/update-city-zones.mjs from the layers below, with the bounds here: each zone is one ring of [lat, lng] points, simplified to within half a metre, or 2 m for Berlin's, Hamburg's and München's no-parking zones and Wien's no-parking and no-riding zones, drawn to the centimetre, and Nashville's parks, 21,000 points at half a metre, and 20 cm for Stockholm's parking places, one of them 70 cm wide. A zone of several parts is a zone for each, and a hole in one, as in five of Västerås's, is drawn by its ring going round the hole and back. Norrköping's map serves its zones only as pictures: they are read from the SVG it draws, to within its 0.5 m pixels for the parking places and 2.75 m for the other zones. Porto gives its parking places as points with their number of spots, so each is drawn as a disc of 5 m around its point, and so are Boise's and Arlington County's parking corrals, those installed, Seattle's bike and scooter corrals, Cleveland's shared mobility hubs, Tampa's multi-use hubs and public bike racks, but for the six it marks secure, five of them racks in its parking garages, Santa Monica's and Sacramento's drop zones, Namur's signed parking places, Poznań's Hop & Go points, Lambeth's parking bays, Ottawa's designated parking, Turku's parking places, Rostock's, Stockholm's five given as points, Augsburg's, Le Chesnay-Rocquencourt's, Lisboa's, Mülheim an der Ruhr's, Phoenix's, Roma's and Vilnius's parking places, Austin's parking boxes and corrals, Denver's corrals, Orlando's designated parking areas, the University of Florida's parking areas, Budapest's Mobi-pontok, Kraków's mobility points, Kassel's bicycle racks, Plymouth's Beryl docking stations, Leeds's Beryl bays and Hamburg's parking areas, marked or at stops; Berlin's are the circles of 10 m it draws round each of its parking places. Ottawa's no-ride roads and pathways are lines, not drawn; nor are Minneapolis's mobility hubs, no places a ride must end. Vantaa's mandatory parking zones and Vaasa's restricted parking area, where a ride may end only at one of the city's parking places, are not drawn, nor are Vantaa's temporary zones for events, nor München's areas and zones set until a day, for building sites or an event, nor Wien's set until a day or for some days only, as the Naschmarkt's flea market on Saturdays. Arlington National Cemetery is no city, but federal rules forbid riding there (32 CFR 553.33(c)(8)): it is drawn as a no-ride zone, its outline from OpenStreetMap (© OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL), credited to both. Boulder's are Lime's, the operator's, credited to it: the City of Boulder's own layer answers scripts only with a challenge, so they are read from the public zone file Lime's rider app draws them from, each zone an encoded polyline, to within about a metre. Its mandatory parking zone, where a ride ends at a Lime corral that the file does not hold, and its two no-riding areas of about 90 km² round the city, where Lime's service area ends, are not drawn. Nagoya's zones are lines instead of a ring: the pavements where a scooter in its 6 km/h mode may ride, rule 81 (普通自転車歩道通行可) of the Aichi police's traffic rules as JARTIC publishes them, those whose middle lies within the city's outline on OpenStreetMap, simplified to within a metre. Only the website draws them; the apps' catalogs leave them out. The map draws them from zoom 14, whether or not the operators' zones are on. Berlin's and Hamburg's, too many to build into the iPhone app, are marked download: the app downloads them when a view reaches the city (docs/city-zone-downloads.md). The website draws them as it does the others.

source.title: City of Tampa, "Don't be an April Fool, follow the new eScooter rules!" (1 April 2024): a shared e-scooter or e-bike is parked only at a city-approved docking station, its marked and virtual corrals, public bike racks, scooter racks and charging stations

source.title: Turun kaupunki, "Sähköpotkulaudat": park a scooter preferably in a place marked for scooters, painted on the ground or a rack, and never in a no-parking area; ride at most 10 or 15 km/h in the speed-limited areas, and not at all in the no-riding areas, which the city keeps up to date on its service map

source.title: JUDU, "Mikrojudumas" (updated 20 May 2026): in the city centre a shared e-scooter or e-bike is left only at a parking place marked for them; in the Old Town and on bridges and viaducts it rides at 12 km/h at most, and signs ban scooters and bikes from Vilniaus, Pilies and Savičiaus gatvės

source.title: District Department of Transportation, "District Shared Fleet Device Laws and Regulations": a shared scooter is parked on the sidewalk, between it and the kerb or at a bike rack or in-street corral, locked, leaving 3 feet clear, and not ridden on the sidewalk in the Central Business District; the zones where it may not be parked or ridden, or only slowly, are among the rules operators must keep to. The no-parking zones and the corrals are the District's open data (CC BY 4.0)

map.title: Stadt Wien, "E-Scooter-Beschränkungszonen Wien" (open data)
